subject: Lighting and power for productive work
hook: Facing the window or side-on to it? One choice changes your whole working day.
ig:
Facing the window or side-on to it? One choice changes your whole working day.

It's the first thing we ask when planning a fitted desk, because it decides where the grommets, shelving and task light go.

A: Facing the window
You get the view and good daylight on your face for video calls. The trade-off: a bright window directly behind your screen makes your eyes work harder, especially on winter mornings when the sun is low.

B: Side-on to the window
Glare drops right down and light falls evenly across the worktop. The trade-off: you lose the view unless you turn your head.

Facing away from the window is the one we usually steer people off, because the screen reflects the whole window back at you.

Which would you choose, and why? Tell us in the comments: A or B plus the reason. Room shape often decides it, so mention yours.
fb:
Quick one for anyone setting up a home office this January: should the desk face the window, or sit side-on to it?

Facing it gives you the view and lovely light for video calls, but the bright window behind your screen can be tiring on the eyes. Side-on cuts the glare and lights the desk evenly, but you'll miss the view.

We ask this at the start of every home office design because it decides where everything else goes.
